 succeeded in 0ms:
     1	import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
     2	import type { z } from 'zod';
     3	import { calloutCore } from '../core/core-definition';
     4	import { VARIANT_ICONS } from './icons';
     5	import { VARIANT_TOKENS, type Variant } from './variant-tokens';
     6	
     7	type CalloutProps = z.infer<typeof calloutCore.propsSchema>;
     8	
     9	export interface CalloutBodyProps {
    10	  readonly props: CalloutProps;
    11	  readonly children: ReactNode;
    12	}
    13	
    14	/**
    15	 * Visual primitive shared by `CalloutEditorView` and `CalloutRenderView`. The
    16	 * two views differ only in how they hand `children` in (Tiptap-managed inner
    17	 * node vs. static SSR content); the DOM/class shape MUST match byte-for-byte
    18	 * so the editor preview and the published page render identically.
    19	 *
    20	 * Visual rules live in `./callout.css` (gated on `data-callout-variant`).
    21	 */
    22	export function CalloutBody({ props, children }: CalloutBodyProps): ReactNode {
    23	  const variant: Variant = props.variant;
    24	  const tokens = VARIANT_TOKENS[variant];
    25	  const Icon = VARIANT_ICONS[variant];
    26	  const heading = props.title ?? tokens.label;
    27	
    28	  return (
    29	    <aside
    30	      role="note"
    31	      aria-label={`${tokens.label} callout`}
    32	      data-callout-variant={variant}
    33	      tabIndex={0}
    34	    >
    35	      <span className="skb-callout-icon" aria-hidden="true">
    36	        <Icon />
    37	      </span>
    38	      <div className="skb-callout-body">
    39	        <strong className="skb-callout-title">{heading}</strong>
    40	        <div className="skb-callout-content">{children}</div>
    41	      </div>
    42	    </aside>
    43	  );
    44	}

     1	import type { z } from 'zod';
     2	import type { ColorTokenName } from '@skb/design-tokens';
     3	import { calloutCore } from '../core/core-definition';
     4	
     5	type Variant = z.infer<typeof calloutCore.propsSchema>['variant'];
     6	
     7	interface VariantSpec {
     8	  readonly label: string;
     9	  /** Design-token color name driving the accent bar + icon glyph. */
    10	  readonly accentToken: ColorTokenName;
    11	}
    12	
    13	/**
    14	 * Variant → design-token mapping. The `ColorTokenName` constraint binds this
    15	 * file to `@skb/design-tokens`'s public color token surface: renaming or
    16	 * removing a color token here is a static type error.
    17	 *
    18	 * Visual styles for these variants live in `./callout.css` (selector
    19	 * `[data-callout-variant="..."]`); this file is the single-source of variant
    20	 * metadata consumed by both the React tree and any future style-introspection
    21	 * tooling.
    22	 */
    23	export const VARIANT_TOKENS: Readonly<Record<Variant, VariantSpec>> = {
    24	  note: { label: 'Note', accentToken: 'note' },
    25	  tip: { label: 'Tip', accentToken: 'success' },
    26	  warning: { label: 'Warning', accentToken: 'warn' },
    27	  danger: { label: 'Danger', accentToken: 'error' },
    28	};
    29	
    30	export type { Variant };

     1	import type { ZodTypeAny, infer as ZodInfer } from 'zod';
     2	import type { ComponentType } from 'react';
     3	
     4	export type BlockKind = 'prose' | 'component' | 'render' | 'viz';
     5	
     6	/**
     7	 * BlockCore：headless 层 —— 无 React 依赖，纯逻辑（props schema + MDX 序列化在
     8	 * mdx-bridge 处理）。Core 可被 Adopter 复用并配自定义 UI。
     9	 */
    10	export interface BlockCoreDefinition<TSchema extends ZodTypeAny = ZodTypeAny> {
    11	  /** kebab-case identifier，全局唯一 */
    12	  readonly name: string;
    13	  readonly kind: BlockKind;
    14	  readonly propsSchema: TSchema;
    15	  /** MDX 中实际使用的 PascalCase 组件名，例如 "Callout" / "JupyterBlock" */
    16	  readonly mdxComponent: string;
    17	}
    18	
    19	export interface BlockViewProps<TSchema extends ZodTypeAny> {
    20	  readonly props: ZodInfer<TSchema>;
    21	  readonly content?: string;
    22	  /** Wave 2 起追加 runtime context（kernel session / theme / etc.） */
    23	}
    24	
    25	/**
    26	 * BlockUI：presentational 层 —— React 组件，绑定到已注册的 core。
    27	 * 同一 core 可挂多个 UI（uiId 区分），Adopter 可写自己的 UI 替代 ui-default。
    28	 */
    29	export interface BlockUIDefinition<TSchema extends ZodTypeAny = ZodTypeAny> {
    30	  /** 必须指向已 registerCore 的 core */
    31	  readonly coreName: string;
    32	  /** UI 实现 id：'default' / 'minimal' / 用户自定义 */
    33	  readonly uiId: string;
    34	  readonly EditorView: ComponentType<BlockViewProps<TSchema>>;
    35	  readonly RenderView: ComponentType<BlockViewProps<TSchema>>;
    36	}
    37	
    38	export function defineCore<T extends ZodTypeAny>(
    39	  def: BlockCoreDefinition<T>,
    40	): BlockCoreDefinition<T> {
    41	  return def;
    42	}
    43	
    44	export function defineUI<T extends ZodTypeAny>(
    45	  def: BlockUIDefinition<T>,
    46	): BlockUIDefinition<T> {
    47	  return def;
    48	}
    49	
    50	/**
    51	 * BlockRegistry：双层注册表（ADR-0003）。
    52	 * registerCore：挂业务定义；registerUI：挂视觉实现。
    53	 * 同 core 多 UI 场景：getUI(name) 不带 uiId 时取首个注册的（约定为 'default'）。
    54	 */
    55	export class BlockRegistry {
    56	  readonly #cores = new Map<string, BlockCoreDefinition>();
    57	  readonly #uis = new Map<string, BlockUIDefinition[]>();
    58	
    59	  registerCore(core: BlockCoreDefinition): void {
    60	    if (this.#cores.has(core.name)) {
    61	      throw new Error(`Duplicate core name: ${core.name}`);
    62	    }
    63	    this.#cores.set(core.name, core);
    64	  }
    65	
    66	  registerUI(ui: BlockUIDefinition): void {
    67	    if (!this.#cores.has(ui.coreName)) {
    68	      throw new Error(`Unknown core for UI registration: ${ui.coreName}`);
    69	    }
    70	    const existing = this.#uis.get(ui.coreName) ?? [];
    71	    if (existing.some((u) => u.uiId === ui.uiId)) {
    72	      throw new Error(
    73	        `Duplicate UI registration: core=${ui.coreName} uiId=${ui.uiId}`,
    74	      );
    75	    }
    76	    existing.push(ui);
    77	    this.#uis.set(ui.coreName, existing);
    78	  }
    79	
    80	  getCore(name: string): BlockCoreDefinition | undefined {
    81	    return this.#cores.get(name);
    82	  }
    83	
    84	  listCores(): readonly BlockCoreDefinition[] {
    85	    return [...this.#cores.values()];
    86	  }
    87	
    88	  /** 不传 uiId 时返回首个（约定为 'default'）；传了精确匹配 */
    89	  getUI(coreName: string, uiId?: string): BlockUIDefinition | undefined {
    90	    const list = this.#uis.get(coreName);
    91	    if (!list || list.length === 0) return undefined;
    92	    if (uiId === undefined) return list[0];
    93	    return list.find((u) => u.uiId === uiId);
    94	  }
    95	
    96	  listUIs(coreName: string): readonly BlockUIDefinition[] {
    97	    return [...(this.#uis.get(coreName) ?? [])];
    98	  }
    99	}

     1	# @skb/block-foundation Contract
     2	
     3	## Public surface
     4	
     5	- `BlockRegistry` class — 双层注册表（ADR-0003）
     6	  - `registerCore(core)` / `registerUI(ui)`
     7	  - `getCore(name)` / `listCores()`
     8	  - `getUI(coreName, uiId?)` / `listUIs(coreName)`
     9	- `defineCore(def)` / `defineUI(def)` factory helpers
    10	- `BlockCoreDefinition<T>` / `BlockUIDefinition<T>` / `BlockViewProps<T>` interfaces
    11	- `BlockKind = 'prose' | 'component' | 'render' | 'viz'` （四分类，Wave 2 由 2→4 additive 扩展）
    12	  - `'prose'` — Wave 1 default for headless prose blocks (无 MDX 组件，由 `proseExtensions` 提供 markdown 行为)
    13	  - `'component'` — Wave 1 for MDX-component blocks（block-callout / block-code / block-image — Track C simple-block-eng）
    14	  - `'render'` — **Wave 2 NEW** for hand-crafted render blocks consuming external runtime authority（block-math KaTeX / block-pdf react-pdf — Track D render-block-eng）
    15	  - `'viz'` — **Wave 2 NEW** for visualization blocks consuming heavy runtime libs（block-jupyter Pyodide / block-nn-viz TensorFlow.js / block-agent-flow React Flow — Track E viz-block-eng / kernel consumer）
    16	- `proseExtensions` — Tiptap 扩展数组，提供全部 markdown 行为
    17	
    18	## Invariants
    19	
    20	- `BlockKind` 四分不可破坏：新 block 必须明确归属 `prose` / `component` / `render` / `viz` 之一。Wave 1 仅 `prose` + `component` 二分；Wave 2 additive 扩展加 `render` + `viz`（由 `render-block-eng` 与 `viz-block-eng` 工种 own，与 agent-contract.md Tier 1 worker 分工一致）。kind 定义不可被进一步窄化（不允许把 `render` 重新归并入 `component`），扩展再加 kind 需 ADR
    21	- Prose blocks 零自写代码——任何看似需要新 prose block 的场景应通过组合 `proseExtensions` 内现有扩展或追加单条 Tiptap 扩展实现，不再加 prose-kind block
    22	- `BlockCoreDefinition.mdxComponent` 必须 PascalCase，且与 MDX 文件 import 中使用的名字一致
    23	- Core 与 UI 物理分离（ADR-0003）：core 不允许 import 任何 React/Tiptap 视觉 API；UI 必须 import core（不允许 inline 重复 schema）
    24	- 同 core 多 UI 时 `getUI(name)` 取首个注册：约定首个 uiId 为 `'default'`；adopter 在 register 顺序上需谨慎
    25	- **Defensive copy**：`listCores()` 与 `listUIs(coreName)` 每次返回 fresh array。Caller 修改返回值不影响 registry 内部 state。Implementation: `src/registry.ts:84` (`listCores`) + `src/registry.ts:96` (`listUIs`)；regression: `src/__tests__/registry.test.ts` "listCores returns a defensive copy" + "listUIs returns a defensive copy"
    26	- **Idempotent register**：`registerCore` 同 `name` 第二次调用 throws `Duplicate core name: <name>`；`registerUI` 同 `(coreName, uiId)` 第二次 throws `Duplicate UI registration: core=<coreName> uiId=<uiId>`。避免 silent override；实现见 `src/registry.ts:60-63` + `src/registry.ts:71-75`
    27	- **Schema strictness**：每个 `BlockCoreDefinition.propsSchema` 必须是 `z.object(...).strict()`；嵌套 `ZodObject` 同样必须 `.strict()`（[ADR-0006](../../docs/decisions/ADR-0006-asymmetry-audit-checklist.md) item #3 trip-hazard：`.strict()` 不传播）。当前类型仅约束到 `ZodTypeAny`（type-narrow 到 `ZodObject` 待 Wave 3）；Wave 2 行为约定 + reviewer + RFC.md §1 显式提醒。未 `.strict()` 不会 throw，但 `propsSchema.parse(input)` 会 silently strip unknown keys，引发 contract drift
    28	- **Serialize / parse hook ownership**：MDX serialize/parse 由各 `block-*` 包的 `core/` own（ADR-0003 D1+D2），不在 `block-foundation` 注册。`block-foundation` 仅 own `BlockCoreDefinition` 形状（含 `mdxComponent` 字符串）；`mdx-bridge` 通过 `mdxJsxFlowElement.name` 字符串路由到对应 block 的 export（命名约定 verb-as-prefix：`serialize<BlockName>` / `parse<BlockName>`，与 mdx-bridge 现有 `mdxToTiptap` / `tiptapToMdx` 同 style）。详见 RFC.md §"5. Serialize / parse hook ownership"
    29

    12	- `STORAGE_KEY` — `'skb-theme'`; the localStorage key shared with the inline FOUC script
    13	- `ThemeToggle` — default switch button component
    14	- `themeNames` / `ThemeName` / `UseThemeResult` — type-level surface
    15	
    16	## Invariants (ADR-0003)
    17	
    18	- **CSS var names are stable**: consumers (apps/site, every block ui-default) depend on the literal var names; renaming is a contract break and requires an ADR.
    19	- **Light + dark must share the same key set**: only values may differ. Adding a new var REQUIRES adding it to both files at the same time.
    20	- **`STORAGE_KEY` is shared with apps/site BaseLayout**: the inline FOUC `<script>` reads `'skb-theme'` literally; any rename must update both packages in the same PR.
    21	- **Tailwind preset is the single source of truth**: `apps/site` and every `block-*/ui-default/` MUST consume this preset. Hand-rolling `theme.colors` or hard-coding color / spacing / typography values is rejected by `pr-gate`.
    22	- **Persistence is coupled to manual user action only** (ADR-0003 D6): `useTheme`'s mount effect calls `applyThemeDOM` only — it never writes localStorage. Persistence happens in `setTheme` / `toggle`. This preserves the property "system OS theme change is reflected on next visit unless the user has explicitly chosen a theme."
    23	
    24	## Inverse-direction obligation: replicas of pre-hydration algorithms
    25	
    26	Some algorithms in this package must be replicated in inline code that runs **before any module loads** (e.g. an Astro `<script is:inline>` in `<head>` that prevents FOUC), and therefore cannot import from `@skb/design-tokens`. Those replicas carry an inverse-direction obligation: the authority lives here, but the correctness contract binds every consumer that ships its own copy.
    27	
    28	**Currently in scope**: `getInitialTheme()` in `src/use-theme.ts` (the boot-theme derivation: localStorage → `prefers-color-scheme` → `'light'` default).
    29	
    30	Any consumer that replicates this algorithm in inline code MUST be byte-equivalent to the authority in BOTH happy-path AND exception handling:
    31	
    32	1. **Strict-whitelist saved value**: only `saved === 'light' || saved === 'dark'` honors the stored value; anything else falls through to `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')`. A truthy-coerce check (e.g. `saved ? saved === 'dark' : ...`) diverges for invalid / case-mismatched / legacy localStorage values and produces a hydration flash on first paint.
    33	2. **Narrow `try/catch` scope**: the `try/catch` MUST wrap ONLY the `localStorage.getItem` call. `matchMedia` + DOM apply MUST run AFTER the catch handler. A wide-scope `try/catch` swallows the `matchMedia` path on Safari Private Mode / iOS WebView with storage restrictions / browsers with localStorage disabled — producing light when system pref is dark, i.e. hydration flash.
    34	3. **Hardcoded storage key literal**: replicas hardcode `'skb-theme'` (the value of `STORAGE_KEY` in `src/use-theme.ts`) because they cannot import the constant at FOUC-script time. Renaming `STORAGE_KEY` is a contract break that requires updating every replica in the same PR.
    35	
    36	**Required regression test**: every consumer with an inline replica MUST register a test that asserts byte-equivalence against the authority. Template: `apps/site/src/__tests__/fouc-script.test.ts` — extracts the IIFE from the consumer file, evaluates it via `new Function('localStorage', 'window', 'document', iife)` against parametrized fakes, compares output against `getInitialTheme()` for a 16-row saved-value × system-preference corpus + 2 storage-throws × system-preference rows + 1 truthy-coerce regression assertion (20 tests total). The two storage-throws rows are critical: the saved-value corpus alone passes under a wide-scope `try/catch`.
    37	
    38	**Failure mode reference**: Track A v1 review caught happy-path divergence (truthy-coerce); v2 fixed (1) but kept wide-scope `try/catch`; v3 fixed (2). Both v1 and v2 would have shipped visible hydration flash without pr-gate's catch.
    39	
    40	**Current consumers**: `apps/site` (Wave 1, `src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro`). Wave 2+ consumers (e.g. additional Astro apps, future open-source `apps/demo`) MUST follow this template.
    41	
    42	## Consumer rules
    43	
    44	- **Hydration**: `useTheme` and `ThemeToggle` MUST be used inside a client-only Astro island (`client:load` minimum). The hook reads `window.matchMedia` and `window.localStorage` at first render — passive SSR markup is fine, but island hydration directive must be `client:load` or stricter.
    45	- **FOUC bridge** (apps/site responsibility): the BaseLayout `<script is:inline>` in `<head>` must read `localStorage.getItem('skb-theme')` literally, fall back to `matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches`, and set `data-theme="dark"` on `<html>` accordingly — **before** any React island hydrates. The inline script must NOT write localStorage. The detailed correctness obligation (algorithm + try/catch scope + literal sync + required regression test) is enumerated in the **Inverse-direction obligation** section above.
    46	
    47	### `block-*/ui-default/` consumer norms (Wave 2, anchored by `block-callout` C2)
    48	
    49	These norms apply to every `packages/block-*/src/ui-default/` consumer. The
    50	first consumer (`@skb/block-callout/ui-default/`) is the canonical template;
    51	codex-block-generator clones must preserve them.
    52	
    53	- **No hardcoded color literals**: every `color`, `background-color`, `border-color`
    54	  in `*.css` MUST resolve via `rgb(var(--color-X))` or `rgb(var(--color-X) / <alpha>)`.
    55	  No `#hex`, no named colors, no `rgb(<numeric-triple>)`. `pr-gate` greps for
    56	  these in `packages/block-*/src/ui-default/*.css` and rejects.
    57	- **No inline `style={{ … }}` for variant colors**: happy-dom (used by `vitest run`)
    58	  rejects `rgb(var(--color-…))` in inline styles and silently drops the attribute,
    59	  which would mask real visual regressions. Variant colors MUST live in `*.css`,
    60	  selected by `[data-<block>-variant="…"]` on a stable container element. Inline
    61	  `style` is allowed only for layout-time computed values (e.g., a known px width).
    62	- **Type-only `@skb/design-tokens` import satisfies ADR-0008 D1**: `block-*/ui-default/`
    63	  packages typically don't need `colorVars` / `tokens` at runtime (CSS does the var
    64	  resolution). To keep `@skb/design-tokens` as a real `package.json#dependencies` entry
    65	  (per ADR-0008 D1), import the `ColorTokenName` type to constrain the variant→token
    66	  mapping (see `block-callout/src/ui-default/variant-tokens.ts`). The lexical
    67	  `from '@skb/design-tokens'` in source is what the structure-auditor monthly grep
    68	  detects; type-only imports under `verbatimModuleSyntax: true` count.
    69	- **Tailwind preset is consumed at app-build, not block-build**: `block-*` packages
    70	  don't compile Tailwind themselves; `apps/site` (and any future Astro/Next consumer)
    71	  loads `@skb/design-tokens/tailwind-preset` and JIT-compiles the class names that
    72	  `block-*/ui-default/` Components emit. Block packages MAY emit Tailwind utility
    73	  classes (e.g., `mt-1`, `flex`) but those classes resolve correctly only when the
    74	  consumer's Tailwind config extends from this preset. For visual rules that must
    75	  work outside Tailwind (e.g., editor-shell standalone preview), put them in the
    76	  block's own `*.css` file with explicit `var(--space-X)` references.
    77	- **Required CSS import path**: each `block-*` package exposes its CSS via
    78	  `package.json#exports['./ui-default/<block>.css']`. App entry MUST import each block's
    79	  CSS once at boot (next to design-tokens' `tokens.css` + `tokens-dark.css`).
    80	- **No emoji as icons**: `VARIANT_ICONS` (or equivalent) MUST be hand-traced SVGs at
    81	  consistent stroke width (1.5–2px) and consistent viewBox (`24 24`). Mixing
    82	  filled/outlined or different stroke widths violates ui-ux-pro-max
    83	  `no-emoji-icons` + `stroke-consistency` + `icon-style-consistent` rules.
    84	- **A11y on the variant container**: emit `role="note"` (or appropriate landmark),
    85	  `aria-label="<Variant> <block>"`, `tabindex="0"` so the block participates in
    86	  keyboard nav. `:focus-visible` styles in `*.css` MUST use `outline` (not
    87	  `box-shadow` — `outline` survives `forced-colors` mode).
    88	- **Light + dark parity**: any color expression MUST resolve correctly under both
    89	  themes via the design-tokens var system. No theme-specific class branches in
    90	  `block-*/ui-default/`; if a token doesn't exist in both themes, propose adding
    91	  it to `tokens.css` + `tokens-dark.css` per "Modifying this file" below.
    92	- **Reduced-motion**: any `transition` / `animation` MUST be wrapped in
    93	  `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { … }` (see callout.css Wave 2 pattern).
    94	
    95	## Modifying this file
    96	
    97	- Adding a new var: non-breaking, but must update tokens.css + tokens-dark.css + tokens.ts + tailwind-preset.cjs in the same change.
    98	- Renaming or repurposing an existing var (semantic redefinition): contract break — requires an ADR plus a notification to all consuming packages.
    99	- Adding a new theme beyond light/dark (e.g. sepia, high-contrast): requires an ADR; `STORAGE_KEY` value type expands; downstream FOUC scripts must handle the new value.
   100	- Renaming or removing any exported function/component: contract break — requires an ADR. (Pre-Wave-1 the only such rename was `applyTheme` → `applyThemeDOM` to enforce the persistence-coupled-to-manual-action invariant; package had no external consumers.)
   101	
   102	## Related
   103	
   104	- [ADR-0003 headless / presentational split](../../docs/decisions/ADR-0003-headless-presentational-split.md) — D6 (manual-only persistence)
   105	- [Design spec §1.5 / §2.5 / §2.6](../../docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-29-self-knowledge-base-design.md)
   106	- `../block-foundation/CONTRACT.md` — block UI registration depends on this preset
   107	- `../../apps/site/CONTRACT.md` — FOUC inline script literal sync constraint

/bin/bash -lc "nl -ba docs/decisions/ADR-0006-asymmetry-audit-checklist.md | sed -n '46,130p'" in /home/weiyi/selfKnowledgeBaseWeb
 succeeded in 0ms:
    46	Adopt an **8-point asymmetry-audit checklist** as a mandatory part of `code-reviewer` (Codex 5.3-spark, default cheap) and `pr-gate` (Codex 5.5, deep) review prompts. Reviewers MUST work through every applicable item before declaring PASS.
    47	
    48	### The 8 items
    49	
    50	1. **Field/attribute audit**: After adding a field to a data shape (Zod schema, Pydantic model, TS interface, mdast attrs, etc.), audit every comparator / equality / serialization / canonicalization function that handles this shape. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #4 — `marksEqual` link branch missed `title` when serialize emitted it.)
    51	
    52	2. **Status code audit**: After adding a status code to one HTTP handler (or, generally, an exit/error code to one branch), audit every other handler emitting the same code. RFC-mandated headers (RFC 7235 `WWW-Authenticate` on 401, RFC 7231 `Allow` on 405) attach to **the status code itself**, not the framework code path that emitted it. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #2 — custom `SkbError` 401 path missed `WWW-Authenticate`.)
    53	
    54	3. **Strictness audit**: After adding `.strict()` (Zod) / `extra='forbid'` (Pydantic) at one level of an object schema, audit every nested object/sub-schema. The strictness setting **does not propagate**; nested objects must opt in independently. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #3 — top-level `.strict()` shipped while nested `frontmatterSchema` still silently stripped unknown keys.)
    55	
    56	4. **Consumer schema audit**: After defining a schema in a single-authority package (e.g. `@skb/content-types/frontmatterSchema`), audit every consumer for inline duplicates or inline redefinitions that should `import` instead. The "deferred swap" pattern — "I'll inline now and import later" — is a contract break that compounds over time. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #6 part 2 — apps/site/content.config.ts inlined `z.object(...)` rather than importing `frontmatterSchema`.)
    57	
    58	5. **Algorithm + runtime constant replication audit**: When an algorithm or runtime constant is replicated outside its authority (e.g. inline FOUC scripts, login challenge derivation, pre-hydration boot logic that cannot import from packages), audit every consumer-side replica for byte-equivalent reproduction. The replica must register a **regression test** that asserts equivalence against the authority across a representative input corpus. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #6 part 1 — FOUC IIFE truthy-coerce vs `getInitialTheme()` strict-whitelist; remediated with `apps/site/src/__tests__/fouc-script.test.ts` 16-row corpus.)
    59	
    60	6. **Sister-file documentation audit**: After updating one CONTRACT.md (or any document that describes a code surface), audit ALL related CONTRACT.md files in the package family for sister-file drift. Two CONTRACT.md files that describe two halves of the same contract must use **identical terminology** for the shared identifiers (function names, schema names, refine predicate names). (Wave 1 evidence: instance #5 — `editor-commands/CONTRACT.md` updated to cite `editBlockInputSchema` while `agent-tools/CONTRACT.md` still referred to the old shape.)
    61	
    62	7. **Exception-scope equivalence audit**: When replicating an algorithm + its exception handling across files, audit BOTH the happy-path semantics AND the `try/catch` scope between authority and replica. Narrow vs wide `try/catch` can produce divergent fall-through behavior even with identical happy-path logic. Specifically: when `localStorage` / `sessionStorage` / `IndexedDB` / `matchMedia` / any browser API in the algorithm path can throw, the `try/catch` MUST wrap ONLY the throwing call, with the fall-through branch (matchMedia / system default / DOM apply) running AFTER the catch handler — not inside it. (Wave 1 evidence: instance #7 — FOUC IIFE wide-scope try/catch swallowed matchMedia exceptions; remediated with narrow try/catch + 2 storage-throws regression tests.)
    63	
    64	8. **Authority-document → generated/consumed surface audit**: When updating an authority document (ADR, spec, `agent-contract.md`, runbook, CONVENTIONS) **OR a dependency authority (`package.json`)** that mandates behavior in downstream consumers, audit every consumer-side replica/generated artifact for synchronized update **AND staged-in-the-git-index in the same bundle**. Specifically: an ADR section that says "X file MUST be updated to do Y" requires the same commit to update X and provide a way to verify the synchronization. Generated artifacts (e.g. `docs/review-checklist.md` and `.claude/agents/*.md` derived from `agent-contract.md`; **`pnpm-lock.yaml` derived from `package.json`** — see sub-form C below) MUST be regenerated via the documented codegen step (`pnpm generate:configs` / `pnpm install`) AND **explicitly `git add`'d** so the git **index** (not just the working tree) contains the new content; runbooks (`docs/runbooks/team-operations.md`) MUST be cross-linked; Codex/Claude subagent prompt files MUST embed or reference the new rule.
    65	
    66	   **Operational sequence** (do not skip steps):
    67	   ```bash
    68	   # 1. Edit authority + generator code
    69	   # 2. Run codegen
    70	   pnpm generate:configs
    71	   # 3. Stage regenerated outputs (CRITICAL — see Pitfall below)
    72	   git add <regenerated/path/foo.md> <regenerated/path/bar.md>
    73	   # 4. Verify index reflects content (NOT just working tree):
    74	   git diff --cached --stat -- <regenerated paths>
    75	   #    → expects non-empty diff with the expected line counts
    76	   # 5. Verify idempotence: re-run codegen + confirm working tree matches index:
    77	   pnpm generate:configs
    78	   git status --short -- <regenerated paths>
    79	   #    → expects column-1 'M' (staged) + column-2 blank (working tree clean)
    80	   ```
    81	
    82	   **Pitfall (this is the load-bearing step)**: `git status --short` shows two columns: column 1 is index-vs-HEAD; column 2 is working-tree-vs-index. After running the generator without `git add`, you see `' M'` (space + M) — **working tree differs from index, but index still matches HEAD**. `git commit` only commits the index. Skipping `git add` means the regenerated content is in your working tree but NOT in the next commit. The bundle would land authority + generator-code changes WITHOUT the regenerated outputs, leaving consumers (Wave 2 reviewers reading `.claude/agents/*.md`) at pre-update content. Use `git diff --cached` (not `git status`) as the canonical staging-verification command — `--cached` shows index-vs-HEAD only, which is what `git commit` will produce.
    83	
    84	   **Pitfall extension — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is a generated artifact too (sub-form C below)**: when the authority is `package.json` (any dependency add / remove / version bump / `@types/*` shift), `pnpm install` regenerates `pnpm-lock.yaml` as a deterministic derived artifact. Skipping `git add pnpm-lock.yaml` produces the same class of failure as skipping `git add .claude/agents/*.md`: working tree has the synced lockfile but the **index** still holds HEAD's stale lockfile, so the bundle ships `package.json` ahead of its lockfile. CI runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from the bundled state, sees the stale lockfile disagreeing with the new `package.json`, and fails install. The same `git diff --cached --stat -- pnpm-lock.yaml` canonical verification applies. (Wave 1 erratum commit `e15ec36`; codified as sub-form C below.)
    85	
    86	   Generated-from-authority files carry their own header comment ("GENERATED FROM agent-contract.md — DO NOT EDIT BY HAND") OR YAML frontmatter declaring authority source — both forms are acceptable. `pnpm-lock.yaml` lacks an explicit header (the format is fixed by pnpm) but is implicitly declared by `pnpm install`'s contract — its authority is `package.json` + the workspace `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.
    87	
    88	   **Wave 1 evidence**: **instance #8** — ADR-0006 v1 commit codified reviewer-prompt mandates but did not update `agent-contract.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md` / regenerate `.claude/agents/pr-gate.md` / cross-link `team-operations.md` / regenerate `docs/review-checklist.md`; pr-gate caught the dogfood failure during R1 review of the close-ceremony bundle, forcing a v2 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form A — pre-regeneration omission)** — v5 bundle updated authority files (`agent-contract.md`, generator code, `team-operations.md` cross-link) but had not run the generator at all post-edit; the 3 regenerated outputs were stale at HEAD content; pr-gate caught this during R2 review, forcing a v6 fix. **instance #12 (sub-form B — staging-vs-working-tree confusion)** — v6 bundle ran the generator (so working tree had new content) but did NOT `git add` the regenerated outputs; the git **index** still held HEAD blob hashes for the 3 generated files; orchestrator confused `git status --short` "M" prefix (working-tree-vs-index) with index-vs-HEAD; pr-gate caught this via `git ls-files --stage` blob-hash comparison during R3 review, forcing the v7 fix that explicitly stages with `git add` + verifies via `git diff --cached`. **instance #12 (sub-form C — lockfile is a generated-from-authority artifact)** — Wave 1 close ceremony commit `e15ec36` ("fix(deps): commit pnpm-lock.yaml for @tailwindcss/typography (lockfile drift)"): the design-tokens erratum (commit `fdc86a8`) added the `@tailwindcss/typography` dependency to `package.json` but did not stage the regenerated `pnpm-lock.yaml`; CI install used the pre-update lockfile, drifted against the new `package.json`, and failed `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Resolution: commit `e15ec36` staged the lockfile separately. Lesson codified: when the authority is `package.json` (any dependency add / remove / version bump), `pnpm-lock.yaml` is the consumer-side generated artifact and must ride the same bundle — the class equivalence to `.claude/agents/*.md` regeneration is exact (deterministic derive + git-index staging required). The four sub-forms of the same item #8 class — pre-regeneration omission, post-regeneration commit-staging confusion, conceptually-correct-but-operationally-incomplete fix, AND lockfile-as-generated-artifact — together motivate the explicit operational sequence and `git diff --cached` canonical verification command codified above.
    89	
    90	### Wave 2 prep notes (forward-compatibility application)
    91	
    92	The 8 items have specific Wave 2 trip-hazards already identified by Wave 1's review record:
    93	
    94	- **Item #1 + Wave 2 attr-bearing marks**: when the first attr-bearing mark beyond `link` is added to mdx-bridge (e.g. `highlight: {color}`, `kbd: {style}`), the worker MUST simultaneously update `wrapMark` AND `marksEqual` AND add a fixture exercising attr-equality + attr-distinction. Default `return true` in `marksEqual` is a silent-drop trap for any attr-bearing mark. (See pr-gate Track C v4 R3 caveat.)
    95	
    96	- **Item #2 + Wave 2 new error categories**: when Wave 2+ adds new HTTP error categories (e.g. `auth-rate-limit`, `kernel-timeout`), each new `SkbError` subclass MUST emit the same RFC-mandated headers as framework-raised peers. Add a unit test asserting header presence per error type. (See `apps/api/CONVENTIONS.md` §5 Pitfall + Pitfall continued.)
    97	
    98	- **Item #5 + Wave 2 client-side replications**: when apps/site adds new client-side algorithm replications (theme variants beyond light/dark, locale negotiation pre-hydration, etc.), the worker MUST audit both saved-value semantics AND try/catch scope against authority. (See `packages/design-tokens/CONTRACT.md` Inverse-direction obligation invariant.)
    99	
   100	- **Item #7 + future inline scripts**: ANY future `<script is:inline>` block in the project that needs pre-hydration replication of a package algorithm MUST follow the FOUC template (narrow try/catch + corpus regression test).
   101	
   102	## Consequences
   103	
   104	### Positive
   105	
   106	- **Catch the failure mode proactively**: Wave 1 evidence shows reviewer-applied checklist would have caught all 12 instances on the first review round (including the close-ceremony dogfood instance #8 + the 4 fix-loop reinforcements), eliminating 12 round-trip cycles
   107	- **Reviewer prompt clarity**: code-reviewer + pr-gate codex profile prompts gain a concrete, enumerable checklist rather than the implicit "look for symmetric counterparts" expectation
   108	- **Worker self-audit**: workers gain a pre-PR checklist they can run before reporting `ready-for-review`, catching their own asymmetries (memory: `feedback_verification_fresh_state.md` showed the verification-rigor lesson; this checklist is the analogous rigor at code-design level)
   109	- **Empirical grounding**: 12 distinct instances spread across 6 tracks + 5 close-ceremony fix iterations make this rule data-driven, not a "best practice" speculation; instances #9-12 reinforce items #6 + #8 specifically through close-ceremony fix-loop evidence
   110	
   111	### Costs
   112	
   113	- **Review-round time**: applying 8-point audit at every review adds ~5-10 minutes per round of code-reviewer + pr-gate runtime. Acceptable trade-off given Wave 1 round-counts (Track F: 5 rounds; Track A: 3 rounds; Track C: 4 rounds; Track D: 4 rounds) — front-loading review thoroughness reduces total cycles
   114	- **Worker prompt overhead**: each spawn prompt now needs a reference to this ADR + the 8-point checklist. Marginal cost.
   115	- **False-positive risk**: items that don't apply (e.g. #2 "status code" doesn't apply to TS-only packages) need to be triaged and skipped. Reviewer profile prompts must explicitly say "skip items not applicable to this PR's scope" to avoid bloat.
   116	
   117	### Risks (mitigated)
   118	
   119	- **Risk**: workers might mechanically check items without thinking, producing false confidence. **Mitigation**: each item enumerates concrete failure modes from Wave 1, not abstract heuristics — easier to apply
   120	- **Risk**: this list might grow unbounded as Wave 2+ surfaces new asymmetry classes. **Mitigation**: ADR amendments are cheap; each new instance produces an ADR-0006 erratum capturing item #N+1. Wave 2 close ceremony reviews instances and adds items as needed.
   121	
   122	## Implementation
   123	
   124	### Reviewer prompt updates
   125	
   126	`code-reviewer` and `pr-gate` profile prompts MUST be updated to:
   127	
   128	1. State the 8-point checklist verbatim (or by reference to this ADR)
   129	2. Require the reviewer's verdict structure to include "asymmetry-audit applied: items {1..8} verdicts: ..."
   130	3. Explicitly mark FAIL if any applicable item is left un-audited

    42	
    43	### D1：dead-dep policy = Option A（tighten）
    44	
    45	**规则**：每个 `package.json#dependencies` / `peerDependencies` 中的 `@skb/*`
    46	工作区依赖**必须**对应至少一个源码 `from '@skb/<pkg>'` import。
    47	forward-compat 意图（"Wave N+1 will consume X"）可在 CONTRACT.md prose 段表达，
    48	但**不在 package.json 占位**。
    49	
    50	**理由（Option A 优于 Option B）**：
    51	
    52	1. **audit invariant 更简洁**：dead-dep = bug，结构审计不必为
    53	   "forward-compat 是合法 dead-dep" 维护特例；structure-auditor 月度可机械化
    54	   `grep` 检查（"package.json `@skb/*` ↔ source import 一一对应"），
    55	   比 CONTRACT 文本对比可靠。
    56	2. **YAGNI**：mdx-bridge / block-foundation 真用上时再加 dep 是同包改动 + 同 PR
    57	   单点 churn；预先占位换来的"少改一行 package.json"不抵 audit 复杂度。
    58	3. **CONTRACT prose 仍可表达意图**：authoring intent 不丢，只是不再让
    59	   `package.json` 同时承担 "runtime fact" + "future plan" 双重语义。
    60	4. **Phase 3 npm publish 反向证据弱**：当前 phase 全部 `private: true`
    61	   workspace 包，npm publish 顾虑是 Phase 3 议题；届时若需 forward-compat 的

    63	   requirement 绑架（CLAUDE.md hard rule "Don't design for hypothetical future"）。

 succeeded in 171ms:
     1	# RFC: How a `block-*` package registers with `@skb/block-foundation`
     2	
     3	> **Audience**: `simple-block-eng` / `render-block-eng` / `viz-block-eng` writing
     4	> `block-callout` / `block-code` / `block-image` / `block-math` / `block-pdf` /
     5	> `block-jupyter` / `block-nn-viz` / `block-agent-flow` cores; `ux-ui-lead`
     6	> writing the matching `ui-default/` halves.
     7	>
     8	> **Authority**: [ADR-0008](../../docs/decisions/ADR-0008-wave-2-entry-policies.md)
     9	> D2 freezes the registration interface as of 2026-04-30 (commit `b3581bc`).
    10	> This RFC is the consumer-facing walkthrough; the public API surface itself
    11	> lives in [`CONTRACT.md`](./CONTRACT.md).
    12	
    13	This RFC is **not** a spec — `CONTRACT.md` is. It is a step-by-step recipe
    14	showing how the first real consumer (`block-callout`, Task C1/C2) wires its
    15	core + UI into a `BlockRegistry`. Subsequent `block-*` PRs follow the same
    16	shape; cloned `block-code` / `block-image` cores (Tasks C3-C5b) inherit
    17	this structure verbatim.
    18	
    19	## 1. core/ side
    20	
    21	`core/` is the headless half (ADR-0003). No React, no Tiptap; just a Zod
    22	schema + identifying metadata. Place it at `packages/<block>/src/core/`
    23	and export through the package's `core` subpath.
    24	
    25	```typescript
    26	// packages/block-callout/src/core/core-definition.ts
    27	import { defineCore, type BlockCoreDefinition } from '@skb/block-foundation';
    28	import { z } from 'zod';
    29	
    30	const propsSchema = z
    31	  .object({
    32	    variant: z.enum(['note', 'tip', 'warning', 'danger']),
    33	    title: z.string().optional(),
    34	  })
    35	  .strict();
    36	
    37	export const calloutCore: BlockCoreDefinition<typeof propsSchema> = defineCore({
    38	  name: 'callout',
    39	  kind: 'component',
    40	  propsSchema,
    41	  mdxComponent: 'Callout',
    42	});
    43	```
    44	
    45	Notes that map directly to `BlockCoreDefinition` fields in
    46	[`src/registry.ts`](./src/registry.ts):
    47	
    48	- `name`: kebab-case, globally unique. Used as the registry key — duplicate
    49	  registration throws `Duplicate core name: <name>` at runtime.
    50	- `kind`: `'prose' | 'component' | 'render' | 'viz'` (4-way Wave 2 union; Wave 1
    51	  was binary `'prose' | 'component'` — additive expansion in Wave 2). Track C
    52	  simple-block-eng owns `'component'` (block-callout / block-code / block-image —
    53	  composable JSX with rich children); Track D render-block-eng owns `'render'`
    54	  (block-math / block-pdf — visual rendering of a pure declarative input via
    55	  external runtime authority like KaTeX or react-pdf); Track E viz-block-eng /
    56	  kernel consumer owns `'viz'` (block-jupyter / block-nn-viz / block-agent-flow —
    57	  interactive visualization with heavy runtime libs). `'prose'` is reserved for
    58	  behaviors covered by `proseExtensions` and is closed to new entries (CONTRACT
    59	  invariant: "Prose blocks 零自写代码").
    60	- `propsSchema`: must be a `z.object(...).strict()`; every nested
    61	  `ZodObject` must independently call `.strict()`. See
    62	  [`CONTRACT.md` § Invariants — Schema strictness](./CONTRACT.md#invariants)
    63	  + [ADR-0006](../../docs/decisions/ADR-0006-asymmetry-audit-checklist.md) item #3
    64	  (`.strict()` does not propagate into nested objects). The current type
    65	  signature `BlockCoreDefinition<TSchema extends ZodTypeAny>` is wider than
    66	  `ZodObject`; type-narrowing is deferred to Wave 3, so for Wave 2 this is
    67	  a behavior contract enforced by RFC + reviewer + integration tests, not
    68	  by TypeScript. Skipping `.strict()` does not throw — `propsSchema.parse`
    69	  silently strips unknown keys, which is exactly the contract-drift class
    70	  this rule prevents.
    71	- `mdxComponent`: PascalCase, must match the JSX tag used in `.mdx` files
    72	  exactly (the MDX bridge uses this string when serializing back). For
    73	  `block-callout`, MDX content reads `<Callout variant="note">…</Callout>`
    74	  so this field is `'Callout'`.
    75	
    76	`defineCore` is a no-op identity helper that exists purely to give TypeScript
    77	inference a hand — the returned object satisfies `BlockCoreDefinition<T>`
    78	with `T` inferred from `propsSchema`. Equivalent to writing the type
    79	annotation manually. `defineUI` (used in §2) is the symmetric helper for
    80	`BlockUIDefinition<T>`; both helpers exist for inference convenience only,
    81	so consumers can write `defineUI({ ... })` without manually spelling
    82	`<typeof calloutCore.propsSchema>`.
    83	
    84	## 2. ui-default/ side
    85	
    86	`ui-default/` is the presentational half. It imports the core (never inline-
    87	redefines its schema — see ADR-0006 item #4: "single-authority schema → audit
    88	every consumer for inline duplicates"), then attaches React components for
    89	the editor and renderer.
    90	
    91	```typescript
    92	// packages/block-callout/src/ui-default/index.ts
    93	import { defineUI, type BlockUIDefinition } from '@skb/block-foundation';
    94	import { calloutCore } from '../core/core-definition';
    95	import { CalloutEditorView } from './editor-view';
    96	import { CalloutRenderView } from './render-view';
    97	
    98	export const calloutUIDefault: BlockUIDefinition<
    99	  typeof calloutCore.propsSchema
   100	> = defineUI({
   101	  coreName: calloutCore.name, // must reference an already-registered core
   102	  uiId: 'default', // convention: first-registered UI is 'default'
   103	  EditorView: CalloutEditorView,
   104	  RenderView: CalloutRenderView,
   105	});
   106	```
   107	
   108	The two view components share the `BlockViewProps<TSchema>` shape from
   109	[`src/registry.ts`](./src/registry.ts):
   110	
   111	```typescript
   112	// packages/block-callout/src/ui-default/editor-view.tsx
   113	import type { ComponentType } from 'react';
   114	import type { BlockViewProps } from '@skb/block-foundation';
   115	import { calloutCore } from '../core/core-definition';
   116	
   117	export const CalloutEditorView: ComponentType<
   118	  BlockViewProps<typeof calloutCore.propsSchema>
   119	> = ({ props, content }) => {
   120	  // props.variant is z-inferred to 'note' | 'tip' | 'warning' | 'danger'
   121	  // props.title is z-inferred to string | undefined
   122	  // content is the optional Tiptap inner content as a string
   123	  return (
   124	    <aside data-variant={props.variant}>
   125	      {props.title ? <strong>{props.title}</strong> : null}
   126	      <div>{content}</div>
   127	    </aside>
   128	  );
   129	};
   130	```
   131	
   132	`RenderView` follows the same shape but renders for static output (Astro
   133	build / SSR path) rather than the editor. UX/visual conventions for the
   134	component itself (tokens, spacing, accessibility) are owned by `ux-ui-lead`
   135	via `packages/design-tokens/CONTRACT.md`; this RFC fixes only the
   136	registration plumbing.
   137	
   138	### Wiring at boot
   139	
   140	`registerCore` must precede `registerUI` for the same `coreName`; otherwise
   141	`registerUI` throws `Unknown core for UI registration: <coreName>`. The
   142	boot path (Wave 3 `editor-shell` / `apps/site` integration) does:
   143	
   144	```typescript
   145	import { BlockRegistry } from '@skb/block-foundation';
   146	import { calloutCore } from '@skb/block-callout/core';
   147	import { calloutUIDefault } from '@skb/block-callout/ui-default';
   148	
   149	const registry = new BlockRegistry();
   150	registry.registerCore(calloutCore);
   151	registry.registerUI(calloutUIDefault);
   152	
   153	// later, render-time lookup:
   154	const ui = registry.getUI('callout'); // returns calloutUIDefault (uiId='default')
   155	const ui2 = registry.getUI('callout', 'minimal'); // exact match by uiId
   156	```
   157	
   158	When multiple UIs are registered for one core, `getUI(name)` without a
   159	`uiId` returns the **first registered** (CONTRACT invariant — convention:
   160	register `'default'` first). `getUI(name, uiId)` does exact match.
   161	
   162	## 3. Consumer-side test template
   163

   165	UI into a fresh registry and verifies the round-trip. This is the minimum
   166	surface; package-specific tests (props validation, schema edge cases, view
   167	rendering) live alongside.
